(Japanese: '''ミュウツーの{{tt|逆襲|ぎゃくしゅう}}''' ''Mewtwo's Counterattack'') is the {{pkmn|manga}} adaptation of the [[M01|movie of the same name]]. The manga was written by [[Toshihiro Ono]].

==Publications==
The manga adaptation of ''Mewtwo Strikes Back!'' has only ever been published in the July 1998 issue of Gekkan CoroCoro Comic and collected in the CoroCoro movie guidebook.

==Plot==
{{OBP|Mewtwo|M01}} defeats the {{p|Charizard}}, {{p|Blastoise}}, and {{p|Venusaur}} of a trio of {{tc|Team Rocket Grunt}}s, calling them weak before demanding they leave their Pokémon with him and get out of his sight. Alone in a room full of screens that show footage around the world, Mewtwo ponders if there is any trainer who can amuse him in battle.

In a city, {{Ash}} is battling [[Raymond]] where his {{AP|Bulbasaur}} narrowly misses an attack from Raymond's {{P|Donphan}} before defeating it with a single {{m|Solar Beam}}. Frustrated at this loss, Raymond sends out his {{p|Machamp}}, {{p|Golem}}, {{p|Venomoth}}, and {{p|Pinsir}} at Ash all at once. {{AP|Pikachu}} unleashes a powerful {{m|Thunderbolt}}, which defeats Raymond's Pokémon and sends him running from his loss. Ash teases him for the one-sided loss, but his victory is cut short when Misty yells at him to get moving or else they will be late for the Pokémon League CoroCoro Cup, which she struggled to get tickets for. Unfortunately, the three were too late when they arrived as the champion of the CoroCoro Cup has just been declared, earning Ash the ire and a punch from Misty.

From the skies, a cloaked Mewtwo arrives and challenges the champion, sending out his cloned Charizard, Blastoise, and Venusaur, who easily defeats the champion's {{p|Rapidash}}, {{p|Cloyster}}, and {{p|Sandslash}}. Mewtwo declares the champion as weak before stealing his three Pokémon, believing that a weak trainer has no use for his Pokémon while declaring himself the strongest Pokémon Trainer in the world, his {{p|Dragonite}} distributing invitations to [[New Island|New Island Pokémon Castle]] before flying off with Mewtwo on its back. The tournament announcer panics from the mysterious Trainer defeating the champion. Ash gets fired up from the existence of such a strong trainer and wants to go to New Island and battle this trainer. 

The [[Team Rocket trio]] spots Mewtwo on Dragonite's back, flying to New Island. [[James]] knows that Team Rocket used to have a secret laboratory on the island, and [[Jessie]] knows that, until six months ago, she had no idea what experiments happened on the island. {{MTR}} claims to know what happened, mocking that the information was above their pay-grade. After being persuaded (by a comic head stretch) by Jessie and James, Meowth explains that the researchers were studying {{OBP|Mew|M01}} until six months ago where the laboratory exploded into flames. The island was abandoned until now where a giant castle was built and its inhabitants is a mystery. Inside New Island, Mewtwo rests where his assistant checks his vitals. Mewtwo questions what he is and if he is a Pokémon, his assistant affirming that he is one biologically before Mewtwo rests.

Three years ago in the Amazon Rainforest within South America, [[Dr. Fuji (anime)|Dr. Fuji]] has finally sighted Mew where he prepares to capture it. Even with a [[Master Ball]], Fuji was unable to capture the elusive Mew who escapes. After calling out to it, Mew turns back and returns to Fuji. The Team Rocket Grunts accompanying Fuji attempt to use the Master Ball at Mew but [[Giovanni (anime)|Giovanni]] orders them to stand down and observe, believing that Mew's {{t|Psychic}}-type properties allows it to read Fuji's heart and see whether it can trust humans. Giovanni's guess turns out to be correct where Mew stays with Dr. Fuji and returns with him to their camp, allowing him to take an eyelash of it for further research.

Giovanni tasks Fuji to use Mew's DNA to create a new Pokémon that is the most powerful, offering full funding of the project at the cost of using Mew as the test subject. Giovanni brings up how Fuji was shunned by the scientific community on a Pokémon Bioengineering Project to manipulate him into going through with the project. Giovanni's words and memories of the scientists who looked down on him and disapproved of his research began to blacken Fuji's heart where he takes up Team Rocket's resources to create a new Pokémon. Sensing this darkness caused Mew to tearfully leave, Fuji pleading it to return. Mew leaving was the last straw which fully engrossed Fuji into his darkness and research where he finally created Mewtwo, the strongest Pokémon designed to surpass Mew.

Mewtwo's power allows it to effortlessly defeat a {{p|Nidoking}}, surpassing Giovanni's expectations where it is given a special armor to control its powers better as it is sent to battle more Pokémon. These results please Giovanni who offers Mewtwo a reward of anything except the removal of its armor which he claims is a symbol of friendship between it and humanity. Mewtwo sees through these lies as it knows the armor was to restrict its power. Mewtwo questions whether what it is doing is right. Giovanni answers that there is no right or wrong as long as they win as history is written by the victors. Giovanni orders Fuji to create an armor that allows it to control its thoughts as Mewtwo's intellect is growing, something Fuji is not comfortable with. What completely shocks Fuji is Giovanni revealing Phase Two of the project which is mass-produced Mewtwos.

Knowing that there is no turning back, Fuji removes the armour and begs Mewtwo to destroy everything in the laboratory, including Fuji himself. Fuji explains that he has lived a life full of hatred until Mewtwo was born, telling Mewtwo that it is a prototype where it will have mass-produced siblings designed for mass destruction with no heart or will. Mewtwo retorts that Fuji taught it that it should work hard for Team Rocket just as Team Rocket Grunts show up and try to arrest Fuji for insubordination. Fuji's last words was thanking Mewtwo for considering him its father as Mewtwo destroys the laboratory. After the big explosion, Mewtwo was alone in the rain as it cried out to the sky, questioning what it should do as a creature born from hatred designed only to fight.

Back in the present day at the [[Pokémon Center]] near the pier, {{OBP|Miranda|M01}} orders all trainers with invitations to turn back from the pier as no boats are going to New Island and that there is no tournament there either. Ash defies the orders and believes he can get through the storm if it means battling the strongest trainer, jumping into the ocean riding his {{AP|Squirtle}}. Misty and a bunch of other trainers follow suit as they ride their own {{t|Water}} Pokémon into the ocean. The manga ends with the trainers braving the storm and Ash telling the reader that to see what happens on New Island, they will need to watch the movie.

==Errors==
* [[Ash's Pikachu]] defeats {{p|Golem}} with {{m|Thunderbolt}}, despite Golem being immune to Electric-type attacks.

==Differences between the movie and the manga==
* In [http://web.archive.org/web/20000510020712/http://www.vizkids.com/pokemon/news_interview.shtml an interview with Animerica magazine], Toshihiro Ono revealed he was instructed to include Mewtwo's origin story in the manga adaptation. Since Ono only had the movie's script to work with (the original theatrical version of the movie was released approximately two months after he had begun work on the manga, with the prologue not being written before the main series hiatus and subsequent episode delays caused by the [[EP038]] incident) and the radio drama [[The Birth of Mewtwo]] had not been created yet, Ono created his own original explanation of Mewtwo's origin.
* Charizardtwo, Blastoisetwo and Venusaurtwo were cloned directly from a Charizard, Blastoise and Venusaur owned by {{tc|Team Rocket Grunt}}s. The origin of their animated series counterparts are unknown.
* Ash battles [[Raymond]] in a city rather than in a grassy field. Raymond has a different design where he wears a baseball cap, shirt and jacket rather than a vest, bandana and holding a cutlass.
* During Ash's battle with [[Raymond]], the match between [[Ash's Squirtle]] and Raymond's {{p|Machamp}} doesn't occur in the manga. Instead, {{AP|Pikachu}} defeats Machamp alongside the {{p|Venomoth}}, {{p|Golem}} and {{p|Pinsir}} like in the movie.
* Instead of sending out invitations to Trainers it selected, Mewtwo hosts a tournament called the "CoroCoro Cup" at the Pokémon Dome and challenges its winner to a battle. After defeating him, it challenges the Trainers in attendance to visit it on [[New Island]] in a week's time. Unlike the movie, Mewtwo steals the Pokémon of the champion rather than doing so at [[New Island]].
* {{TRT|Meowth}} explains the history of [[New Island]] where there used to be a Team Rocket laboratory studying {{OBP|Mew|M01}} before an explosion occurred and that there is now a castle on New Island. Meowth is also treated as the boss of the trio where in the movie and series, the three are equals.
* {{OBP|Mewtwo|M01}} and {{an|Dr. Fuji}} have a closer relationship than they do in the film, with Mewtwo considering Fuji like a father.
* Mewtwo physically talks, using its mouth, instead of through telepathy.
* Dr. Fuji's motivations are different than in the movie. In the manga, he is motivated to clone {{p|Mew}} out of a desire for revenge against an institute he was expelled from.
* Dr. Fuji meets {{OBP|Mew|M01}} face-to-face and befriends it, leading to his acquiring one of its eyelashes. It later leaves him when he becomes consumed by his work.
* Dr. Fuji attempts to {{pkmn2|caught|catch}} Mew using a [[Master Ball]] in the manga. No Master Ball is featured at any point in the movie.
* {{an|Giovanni}}'s ultimate plan is to have Dr. Fuji mass produce Mewtwo and create an army of mindless living weapons. Fuji begs Mewtwo to destroy the laboratory to prevent this and it does so, causing Fuji's death.
* [[Officer Jenny]] isn't featured in the manga, while in the movie, she is seen trying to uphold the peace at [[Old Shore Wharf]] alongside {{OBP|Miranda|M01}}.
* Ash and {{ashfr}} leave Old Shore Wharf on their Pokémon, whereas in the movie, {{TRT}} initially offers them a lift to their destination before they capsize and are forced to swim using their Pokémon.
* Several different Trainers are featured among the many trying to reach New Island, including a girl riding her {{p|Tentacool}}, another girl on a {{p|Goldeen}}, a male Trainer on a {{p|Lapras}}, another male on a {{p|Dewgong}}, and another Trainer with a {{p|Poliwhirl}}.
